assessment.provenance_note: Annual tree-ring 14C measurements and ICCP17 recalibration provide direct empirical basis for 16th century BCE date.
assessment.rationale: The offset from IntCal13 and its correction via ICCP17 moves calibrated dates into the 16th century BCE, directly supporting the assertion that the Thera eruption occurred before 1600 BCE.
limitations: The study's annual data cover 1700–1500 BCE and do not extend beyond this range to confirm earlier dates.
Recalibration effects are sample-specific and depend on calibration curve shape; not all samples shift into the 16th century.
The analysis focuses on calibration curve improvement rather than providing an absolute eruption date.

excerpts.text: Our 285 annual data points are all internally consistent and fall within the 2σ range of most of the raw data underlying IntCal13 (Fig. 1A); however, when compared to IntCal13, both species show a clear and sustained offset in the annual measurements (Fig. 1B) between c.1660 and 1540 BCE.

In each case, the posterior mean based on ICCP17 moves into the 16th century BCE. Furthermore, the younger end of posterior age distribution is considerably extended in all scenarios, magnified by the plateau in the ICCP17 data.

excerpts.text: Measurements of radiocarbon (14C) from legumes and grains (3, 8, 9) buried directly beneath the eruption deposits, and an olive branch (10) buried within them, cluster in the range c.1650–1600 cal BCE relative to the internationally agreed radiocarbon calibration curve, IntCal13 (11), which converts radiocarbon determinations from samples of unknown age into calendar age estimates (12).

Many of the existing radiocarbon determinations have been recalibrated multiple times, with calibrations to older iterations of IntCal [for example, (3, 10)] returning probability distributions ranging into the 16th century because of a slight shift in the position of a well-described (3) radiocarbon plateau in the calibration curve.

excerpts.text: # The Minoan Thera eruption predates Pharaoh Ahmose: Radiocarbon dating of Egyptian 17th to early 18th Dynasty museum objects
The huge volcanic eruption at Thera (Santorini), situated in the Aegean Sea, occurred within the Late Minoan IA archaeological period.
The Minoan eruption is older than the reign of Nebpehtire Ahmose, the first king of the 18th Dynasty, who reunited Upper and Lower Egypt.

Consequently, new Bayesian analyses concerning the time of the Thera eruption were conducted by Manning [60], using the latest IntCal20 calibration curve, which resulted in the following 1σ and 2σ age ranges: 1606–1589 BCE (68.3% probability), 1609–1560 BCE (95.4% probability).

excerpts.text: The most famous one occurred during the Late Minoan IA, an archaeological period traditionally dated from about 1600/1580–1480 BCE [2,3].

When the IntCal98 calibration curve [56], released in 1998, was in use, the Minoan Thera eruption was dated quite early in the 17th century BCE by Bayesian analyses, to ca 1650–1620 BCE [54], and to 1663–1599 BCE [57].

Consequently, new Bayesian analyses concerning the time of the Thera eruption were conducted by Manning [60], using the latest IntCal20 calibration curve, which resulted in the following 1σ and 2σ age ranges: 1606–1589 BCE (68.3% probability), 1609–1560 BCE (95.4% probability).

excerpts.text: The mid-second millennium BCE eruption of Thera (Santorini) offers a critically important marker horizon to synchronize archaeological chronologies of the Aegean, Egypt, and the Near East and to anchor paleo-environmental records from ice cores, speleothems, and lake sediments.

Results show an offset from the international radiocarbon calibration curve, which indicates a shift in the calibrated age range for Thera toward the 16th century BCE. This finding sheds new light on the long-running debate focused on a discrepancy between radiocarbon (late 17th-early 16th century BCE) and archaeological (mid 16th-early 15th century BCE) dating evidence for Thera.
1. The Thera eruption is now dated to the 16th century BCE based on annual radiocarbon data.
